$comment: contentId is expected to echo contentUrl wherever the input omits it. That is the documented default on MediaInfo.contentId and is forced by the platform: GCK Android's MediaInfo.Builder takes contentId as a required constructor argument, so 'unset' cannot be represented, and iOS matches it for parity (see MediaInfo+toGckMediaInfo.kt / MediaInfo+toGckMediaInformation.swift). The round trip is therefore lossy in one direction only -- an omitted contentId is indistinguishable from one explicitly set to contentUrl -- which is the receiver-visible behaviour v4 also had. Same applies to every nested mediaInfo in the other fixture files.

fixtures.$comment: streamType is non-optional in GCK; the GCKMediaInformationBuilder default is Buffered (pinned from observed output), not None. An omitted streamDuration stays omitted on BOTH platforms: Android never sets it (GCK maps that to UNKNOWN_DURATION), and iOS explicitly writes kGCKInvalidTimeInterval rather than leaving the builder default of 0 -- see v5-3mg, where the 0 was observed reaching the wire as "duration":0 against Android's "duration":null.
